def-qft-photon-transverse-space.statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Let
$$\mathcal H=L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf k;\mathbb C^3),\qquad \langle u,v\rangle_2=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\overline{u(\mathbf k)}\cdot v(\mathbf k)\,d^3\mathbf k,$$
with the second-variable-linear convention of [[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]]; the real momentum dot product and norm are those of
[[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. Explicitly extend the real dot product
complex-bilinearly to $a\cdot b=\sum_{j=1}^3a_jb_j$ for $a,b\in\mathbb C^3$.
Each complex fiber instead has the positive Hermitian pairing
$\langle a,b\rangle_2=\overline a\cdot b=\sum_j\overline a_jb_j$ and
norm $\|a\|^2=\sum_j|a_j|^2$; the displayed integral uses this pairing.
Hilbert completeness follows from [[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]. For $\mathbf k\ne0$, write $n(\mathbf k)=\mathbf k/|\mathbf k|$ and
$$P_T(\mathbf k)=I_3-n(\mathbf k)n(\mathbf k)^T.$$
Assign any value at $\mathbf k=0$, which is a Lebesgue-null set. Let $M_{P_T}$ be multiplication by this measurable matrix field and define the positive transverse photon space
$$\mathcal H_T=\operatorname{Ran}M_{P_T} =\{u\in\mathcal H:\mathbf k\cdot u(\mathbf k)=0\text{ for almost every }\mathbf k\ne0\}.$$
The inner product on $\mathcal H_T$ is the restriction of that on $\mathcal H$. Each nonzero momentum fiber is the two-complex-dimensional plane $\{a\in\mathbb C^3:\mathbf k\cdot a=0\}$ perpendicular to the real vector $\mathbf k$ in that Hermitian pairing; no global continuous polarization frame is part of the definition.

def-qft-qed-formal-ring.statement:
For a formal indeterminate $z$, let $\mathbb C\llbracket z\rrbracket$ be the commutative ring of sequences $(a_0,a_1,\ldots)$ written $\sum_{n\ge0}a_nz^n$, with coefficientwise addition and Cauchy-product multiplication. No convergence of a numerical series is part of this definition. For $d\ge1$, matrices over $\mathbb C\llbracket z\rrbracket$ use the usual finite matrix addition and multiplication.

Use the finite graph phase data of [[def-qft-qed-finite-graph-gauge-data]] and the QED $U(1)$, Clifford, and natural-unit conventions of [[def-qft-qed-gauge-data]]. Let $K_0(\zeta)\in GL_d(\mathbb C)$ be an invertible base matrix and let $V(\zeta)\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ be its finite link-hopping matrix. The admissible covariant families satisfy
$$ K_0(\zeta^\theta)=D_\theta K_0(\zeta)D_\theta^{-1},\qquad V(\zeta^\theta)=D_\theta V(\zeta)D_\theta^{-1}. $$
The scalar base $K_0=mI_d$, $m\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}$, is an explicit admissible case. Define
$$ K(z;\zeta):=K_0(\zeta)+zV(\zeta),\qquad S(z;\zeta):=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}(-zK_0(\zeta)^{-1}V(\zeta))^nK_0(\zeta)^{-1}. $$
The coefficient of each power $z^n$ in $S$ is one finite matrix. The item defines this formal candidate; the following lemma proves its two-sided inverse and covariance properties. Define $\det A$ for a finite matrix $A$ over $\mathbb C\llbracket z\rrbracket$ by the Leibniz formula $\det A=\sum_{\sigma\in S_d}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\prod_{j=1}^d A_{j,\sigma(j)}$.

def-qft-qed-photon-energy-multiplier.statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Use the transverse space $\mathcal H_T=\operatorname{Ran}M_{P_T}$ of [[def-qft-photon-transverse-space]], with $P_T(\mathbf k)=I_3-\mathbf n\mathbf n^T$ for $\mathbf k\ne0$ and any assigned value at the null point $\mathbf k=0$. In the QFT length convention, assign $\mathbf k$ units m$^{-1}$ and define the nonnegative measurable multiplier
$$ \omega(\mathbf k):=|\mathbf k|. $$
Its maximal multiplication operator on $\mathcal H_T$ is
$$ (M_\omega f)(\mathbf k):=\omega(\mathbf k)f(\mathbf k),\qquad D(M_\omega):=\{f\in\mathcal H_T:\omega f\in L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf k;\mathbb C^3)\}. $$
Because $\omega$ is a scalar multiplier, $\mathbf k\cdot f(\mathbf k)=0$ a.e. implies $\mathbf k\cdot(M_\omega f)(\mathbf k)=0$ a.e.; thus the displayed multiplication maps its stated domain into $\mathcal H_T$. The value $\omega(0)=0$ is immaterial to the $L^2$ operator. For $\hbar,c>0$, the corresponding one-particle energy convention is $E_1:=\hbar c M_\omega$, in joules.

ex-qft-x04.statement:
Use the massless $m=M=0$ case of the formal tree theorem
[[pthm-qft-example-formal-scattering-decay]] with $s>0$. Explicitly take
incoming $p_1,p_2$ and outgoing $k_1,k_2$ on the positive massless shell,
so each $(E,\mathbf q)$ has $E=|\mathbf q|>0$, with
$p_1+p_2=k_1+k_2=P$ and $h(P,P)=s>0$. Use the theorem's proper
orthochronous center-of-momentum chart $\Lambda P=(\sqrt{s},\mathbf0)$;
$\theta$ is the Euclidean angle between the nonzero spatial parts of
$\Lambda p_1$ and $\Lambda k_1$. The differential
coefficient at $\theta=0$ is twice its value at $\theta=\pi/2$; integrating
over the full sphere gives
$$ \sigma_{\rm coeff}=\frac{4\pi\alpha^2(\hbar c)^2}{3s}. $$
All three quantities are formal coefficients in the adopted map, not event
counts or exact measured cross sections.

ex-qft-x05.statement:
Let $s>0$, dimensionless $\lambda\in\mathbb R$, parent energy
$\mathsf M_0>0$, and
$G_E\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}$ in joules. For scattering, take the incoming $p_1,p_2$ and outgoing $k_1,k_2$
on the positive massless scalar shell, each $(E,\mathbf q)$ having
$E=|\mathbf q|>0$, with common total
$p_1+p_2=k_1+k_2=P$, $h(P,P)=s>0$, and evaluate the coefficient in a
proper orthochronous center-of-momentum chart
$\Lambda P=(\sqrt{s},\mathbf0)$ as in the phase-space supplier.
For decay, take massless positive-shell daughters summing to the rest parent
$P_0=(\mathsf M_0,\mathbf0)$. With these data the identical
final-state quartic total coefficient is
$$ \sigma_{\rm coeff}^{\rm identical} =\frac{\lambda^2(\hbar c)^2}{32\pi s}, $$
and the distinguishable-final coefficient is twice this value. The
identical-daughter decay-rate coefficient is
$$ \Gamma_{\rm coeff}=\frac{|G_E|^2}{32\pi\hbar\mathsf M_0} \quad[\mathrm{s}^{-1}]. $$
Set $\Gamma:=\Gamma_{\rm coeff}>0$. For the lifetime calculation only, let
$(\Xi,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$ be a probability space and let
$T:\Xi\to[0,\infty)$ be a measurable parent lifetime measured in seconds.
Define its law on Borel sets $B\subseteq[0,\infty)$ by
$\mu_T(B):=\mathbb P(T\in B)$, and separately assume that $\mu_T$ has
density $f_T(t)=\Gamma e^{-\Gamma t}$ relative to Lebesgue measure. This is
the additional exponential lifetime model; it gives
$P_{\rm surv}(t):=\mathbb P(T>t)=e^{-\Gamma t}$ for $t\geq0$. Define the
mean lifetime as $\mathbb E[T]:=\int_{[0,\infty)}t\,d\mu_T(t)$, and define
the half-life $t_{1/2}$ by $P_{\rm surv}(t_{1/2})=1/2$. Then the mean
lifetime is $1/\Gamma$ and the half-life is $\ln 2/\Gamma$. The exponential
law is not a consequence of the formal coefficient calculation.

ex-qftmath-x06.statement:
Prescribe one unit charge incoming at rest and outgoing with velocity
$v\mathbf e_z$, where $0<v<1$. The QX08 coefficient is
$$ C(v)=\frac{\alpha}{\pi} \left(\frac1v\log\frac{1+v}{1-v}-2\right)>0. $$
At $v=1/2$ this is
$C=(\alpha/\pi)(2\log3-2)>0$. Set the upper energy cutoff $\Lambda>0$ joules
and lower cutoff $\lambda=\Lambda/e$. The exact model then has sector squared
norms $s_m=e^{-C}C^m/m!$, vacuum-sector squared norm $e^{-C}$, sector-index
sum $C$, and free-energy quadratic expectation
$C\Lambda(1-e^{-1})$ joules. Halving $\lambda$ repeatedly adds
$C\log2$ to the cutoff norm squared at each step; QX08's exact coherent
overlap proof shows that this fixed shell overlap prevents a projective-ray
limit, including arbitrary
phase choices. QX08's separate weak-zero and no-strong-limit claims remain
conditional on its escalated Q8 supplier. The squared norms are mathematical
Hilbert-space quantities, not reported photon probabilities or measured
emissions.

lem-qft-example-cutoff-integrals-and-ser.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and the unit convention of
[[def-qft-example-data]]. Let $\mu,\Lambda,\mu_R>0$ have units
$\mathrm m^{-1}$. For $k\in\mathbb R^4$, $|k|$ is the Euclidean norm and
$\log$ is the natural logarithm. Define the cutoff integral
$$ I_\Lambda=\int_{|k|\le\Lambda} \frac{d^4k}{(2\pi)^4(|k|^2+\mu^2)}. $$
Each term in the subtracted expression has units $\mathrm m^{-2}$.
Then
$$ I_\Lambda= \frac{\Lambda^2-\mu^2\log(1+\Lambda^2/\mu^2)}{16\pi^2}, $$
and the explicitly chosen subtraction has the finite limit
$$ \lim_{\Lambda\to\infty} \left(I_\Lambda-\frac{\Lambda^2}{16\pi^2} +\frac{\mu^2}{16\pi^2}\log\frac{\Lambda^2}{\mu_R^2}\right) =\frac{\mu^2}{16\pi^2}\log\frac{\mu^2}{\mu_R^2}. $$
Separately, let $x\ge0$ be dimensionless and let dimensionless $\lambda\ge0$:
$$ F(\lambda)=\int_0^\infty\frac{e^{-x}}{1+\lambda x}\,dx. $$
For every integer $N\ge0$ the exact finite identity is
$$ F(\lambda)=\sum_{n=0}^{N}(-1)^n n!\lambda^n +(-1)^{N+1}\lambda^{N+1} \int_0^\infty\frac{e^{-x}x^{N+1}}{1+\lambda x}\,dx. $$
The last integral is finite and bounded by $(N+1)!$. The resulting formal
power series $\sum_{n\ge0}(-1)^n n!\lambda^n$ has radius of convergence zero.
The cutoff expression is one evaluated model integral and one chosen
subtraction scheme; it is not a full gauge-invariant QED renormalization
theorem or a continuum-existence claim.

lem-qft-example-four-dimensional-radial-.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For every radius $R>0$ and every
nonnegative Borel function $\varphi:[0,R]\to[0,\infty]$, with extended
Lebesgue integrals and the convention $0\cdot\infty=0$,
$$ \int_{\{x\in\mathbb R^4:\ |x|\le R\}}\varphi(|x|)\,d\lambda_4(x) =2\pi^2\int_0^R\varphi(r)r^3\,dr. $$
In particular, the radial Jacobian and angular factor on a four-dimensional
ball are $r^3$ and $2\pi^2$, respectively.

lem-qft-photon-covariance-spectrum.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. On the future null cone write $p=(\omega,\mathbf k)$, $\omega=|\mathbf k|$, $\mathbf k\ne0$, and use the measure $d\nu=d^3\mathbf k/(2\omega)$. The fiber $p^\perp/\mathbb Cp$ has the positive quotient form of [[lem-qft-photon-null-quotient]]. For each proper orthochronous Lorentz transformation $\Lambda$, the action
$$[s(p)]\longmapsto[\Lambda s(\Lambda^{-1}p)]$$
is a unitary representation on the square-integrable quotient sections. It is strongly continuous. Under the unitary identification with $\mathcal H_T$ given by
$T_p[\epsilon]:=\boldsymbol\epsilon-(\mathbf k/\omega)\epsilon^0$
and $u(\mathbf k)=T_p[s(p)]/\sqrt{2\omega}$, as in [[lem-qft-photon-null-quotient]], the free translation representation has phase $e^{i(\omega a^0-\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf a)}$. Its bosonic Fock lift has joint spectrum the closed future cone
$$\overline V_+=\{(E,\mathbf P):E\ge|\mathbf P|\},$$
with the vacuum at $(0,\mathbf0)$. The energy is the nonnegative sector multiplier $\sum_{r=1}^n|\mathbf k_r|$ with the exact maximal square-integrability domain on each sector and square-summability over sectors. These are mathematical free-field representation statements.

lem-qft-photon-local-field-strength.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Work in the fixed length coordinates $x=(x^0,\mathbf x)\in\mathbb R^4$ with $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and $\eta(v,w)=-v^0w^0+\mathbf v\cdot\mathbf w$; write $\partial_a:=\partial/\partial x^a$. For subsets $S,T\subseteq\mathbb R^4$, say they are **spacelike separated** when $\eta(x-y,x-y)=|\mathbf x-\mathbf y|^2-(x^0-y^0)^2>0$ for every $x\in S$ and $y\in T$. Let $A_0=0$ and let $A_i$ be the transverse potential operator-valued distribution of [[lem-qft-photon-smeared-potential]]. Set
$$F_{ab}=\partial_aA_b-\partial_bA_a,\qquad E_i=-\partial_0A_i,\qquad B_i=\epsilon_{irs}\partial_rA_s,$$
where $\epsilon_{irs}$ is the totally antisymmetric symbol with $\epsilon_{123}=1$. In the commutator formulas below, $\Delta=\sum_{r=1}^3\partial_r^2$ is the spatial Laplacian acting on $x-y$.
For a real antisymmetric test tensor $h=(h^{ab})$ with $h^{ab}\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^4;\mathbb R)$ and $h^{ab}=-h^{ba}$, define
$$F(h)=\frac12\int_{\mathbb R^4}F_{ab}(x)h^{ab}(x)\,d^4x =-A_b(\partial_a h^{ab}).$$
The effective test is conserved, $\partial_b\partial_a h^{ab}=0$, and $F(h)$ is unchanged by $A_b\mapsto A_b+\partial_b\lambda$ for smooth $\lambda$. Its one-particle coefficient $g_h$ is the vector $g_j$ of [[lem-qft-photon-smeared-potential]] for $j_i=-\partial_a h^{ai}$, so $F(h)=a(g_h)+a^\dagger(g_h)$ on $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$.

Let $C_0=-i\Delta_0$, where $\Delta_0$ is the massless scalar causal commutator of [[lem-qft-scalar-causal-commutator]]. As distributions in $x-y$,
$$[E_i(x),E_j(y)]=[B_i(x),B_j(y)] =(-\delta_{ij}\Delta+\partial_i\partial_j)C_0(x-y),$$
$$[E_i(x),B_j(y)]=\epsilon_{jri}\partial_0\partial_rC_0(x-y).$$
Every right-hand side has support in the closed causal cone. Hence compactly supported tests whose supports are spacelike separated in the stated Minkowski sense give commuting field-strength operators on $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$. The quotient representation of [[lem-qft-photon-covariance-spectrum]] makes these smeared field strengths Lorentz covariant: their on-shell coefficient depends on a polarization class only through $p_a\epsilon_b-p_b\epsilon_a$. These conclusions concern gauge-invariant free observables and do not assert locality of the Coulomb potential.

lem-qft-qed-coherent-ir-obstruction.statement:
Use the transverse one-particle space $\mathcal H_T$ and multiplier $\omega(\mathbf k)$ of [[def-qft-qed-photon-energy-multiplier]], and form its symmetric Fock space $\mathcal F_s(\mathcal H_T)$. Let $H_{\rm ph}:=\hbar c\,d\Gamma(\omega)$, with $\hbar,c>0$ and $d\Gamma(\omega)$ acting on the $n$-particle sector as multiplication by $\sum_{j=1}^n|\mathbf k_j|$, as in [[lem-qft-second-quantized-spectrum]]. For a coherent vector use
$$ \epsilon(f):=\bigoplus_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{f^{\otimes n}}{\sqrt{n!}},\qquad C(f):=e^{-\|f\|^2/2}\epsilon(f), $$
using the tensor and direct-sum conventions of [[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]].

Let $\kappa>0$. Let $b:S^2\to\mathbb C^3$ be measurable with $b\in L^2(S^2,d\Omega;\mathbb C^3)$, $\mathbf n\cdot b(\mathbf n)=0$ for a.e. $\mathbf n$, and
$$ C_b:=\int_{S^2}|b(\mathbf n)|^2\,d\Omega>0. $$
Take $\mathbf k,\kappa,\epsilon$ in inverse metres and $b$ dimensionless; then $f_\epsilon$ has momentum-wavefunction units $\mathrm m^{3/2}$, $C_b$ is dimensionless, and $\hbar c(\kappa-\epsilon)$ has energy units.
For $0<\epsilon<\kappa$, define $f_\epsilon(0)=0$ and
$$ f_\epsilon(\mathbf k):=\mathbf1_{\{\epsilon<|\mathbf k|<\kappa\}}|\mathbf k|^{-3/2}b\!\left(\frac{\mathbf k}{|\mathbf k|}\right). $$
Then
$$ \|f_\epsilon\|^2=C_b\log\frac{\kappa}{\epsilon},\qquad \langle C(f_\epsilon),H_{\rm ph}C(f_\epsilon)\rangle =\hbar c\,C_b(\kappa-\epsilon). $$
Each $C(f_\epsilon)$ is a unit vector in $D(H_{\rm ph})$. As $\epsilon\downarrow0$, $C(f_\epsilon)\rightharpoonup0$ weakly, but the family has no strong Fock-space limit. The statement is an exact free transverse-mode construction; it asserts no interacting charged sector, continuum QED limit, or empirical observation.

lem-qft-qed-dirac-gauge-current.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and use the conventions of [[def-qft-qed-gauge-data]]. Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ be open, let each $a_a:U\to\mathbb R$
be a smooth real potential component, and let $\psi:U\to\mathbb C^4$
be a smooth commuting spinor. The real gauge parameter is a smooth
$\alpha:U\to\mathbb R$, and all fields, derivatives and compactly supported
smooth variations below are on this same $U$ (including $U=\mathbb R^4$). Use the symmetrized classical density
$$\mathcal L_D=\frac i2\{\bar\psi\gamma^aD_a\psi-(D_a\bar\psi)\gamma^a\psi\}-\mu\bar\psi\psi,\qquad D_a\bar\psi=\partial_a\bar\psi+ig a_a\bar\psi.$$
For compactly supported smooth variations, its spinor Euler equation is $(i\gamma^aD_a-\mu)\psi=0$ and its adjoint. The density is invariant under the gauge transformation in [[def-qft-qed-gauge-data]]. On solutions,
$$\partial_a j^a=0,\qquad j^a=g\bar\psi\gamma^a\psi.$$
In SI variables the corresponding Hamiltonian density has the sign convention
$$\psi^\dagger\!\left[c\,\boldsymbol\alpha\cdot(-i\hbar\nabla-q\mathbf A)+\beta mc^2+q\phi\right]\psi.$$
These are conditional variational identities for smooth commuting classical fields. They assert no global existence theorem for the coupled field equations, no quantum current product, and no empirical measurement.

lem-qft-qed-formal-matrix-ward.statement:
Let $K(z;\zeta)=K_0(\zeta)+zV(\zeta)$ and $S(z;\zeta)$ be the finite-dimensional formal matrices of [[def-qft-qed-formal-ring]], with $d\ge1$, $K_0(\zeta)$ invertible, and both coefficient matrices covariant under the vertex phase angles of [[def-qft-qed-finite-graph-gauge-data]]. Then $S$ is a two-sided inverse of $K$ in $M_d(\mathbb C\llbracket z\rrbracket)$, and
$$ S(z;\zeta^\theta)=D_\theta S(z;\zeta)D_\theta^{-1} $$
coefficientwise. For a real vertex tuple $\theta$, put
$\Theta:=\operatorname{diag}_{x\in X}(\theta_xI_r)$,
$\zeta_s:=\zeta^{s\theta}$, and $D_s:=D_{s\theta}=e^{is\Theta}$.
Write $K_s:=K(z;\zeta_s)$ and $S_s:=S(z;\zeta_s)$, and define
$\delta K:=\left.\frac{d}{ds}K_s\right|_{s=0}$ and
$\delta S:=\left.\frac{d}{ds}S_s\right|_{s=0}$ coefficientwise along this
differentiable phase path. The variations satisfy
$$ \delta K=i[\Theta,K],\qquad \delta S=i[\Theta,S]=-S(\delta K)S . $$
For ordinary finite matrices $A,B\in GL_d(\mathbb C)$, the corresponding resolvent identity is $B^{-1}(B-A)A^{-1}=A^{-1}-B^{-1}$. These are formal or finite algebraic statements; they assert no convergence of a perturbation series, continuum limit, or loop Ward identity.

post-qft-example-formal-observable-map.statement:
For a specifically named finite tree calculation, adopt its selected formal
diagram coefficient as a **leading perturbative coefficient** with a stated
phenomenological reading. For QED, use the vertex and free-line conventions
of the current draft supplier
[[post-qft-formal-qed-coefficients]]. A particle of natural charge $q_n$ has
vertex $iq_n\gamma^a$; the electron has $q_n=-e_n$ and vertex
$-ie_n\gamma^a$. The rational fermion line is
$$ i\frac{\not p+\mu}{h(p,p)-\mu^2}, $$
for $\mu>0$ and off-shell $p$ with $h(p,p)-\mu^2\ne0$. In Feynman gauge
the auxiliary photon line is
$$ -i\frac{h_{ab}}{h(k,k)+i0}=i\frac{\eta_{ab}}{h(k,k)+i0}. $$
For a finite matrix kernel the coefficientwise inverse in
[[post-qft-formal-qed-coefficients]] is part of the formal convention and
asserts no convergence. If a time-ordered distribution is used, use the
actual free carrier specified there; that identification is conditional on
[[def-countable-choice]]. The displayed pole notation does not define loop
products. In the pair-production channel below the selected muon also has
model charge $-e$, and only the photon line is internal.

For declared incoming spin probabilities, sum over declared final spin
labels, and a specified formal amplitude $\mathcal A$, adopt the
cross-section coefficient map of
[[lem-qft-example-two-body-phase-space]]. Its scattering inputs are
positive-shell energy vectors $p_i=(E_i,\mathbf p_i)$ with
$E_i=\sqrt{|\mathbf p_i|^2+\mathsf M_{i,\rm in}^2}>0$,
$\mathsf M_{i,\rm in}\ge0$, and common future-timelike total
$P=p_1+p_2=k_1+k_2$. The outgoing $k_j$ are on their specified positive
shells. Require $s=h(P,P)>(\mathsf M_1+\mathsf M_2)^2$ for the outgoing
rest energies and positive incoming flux $F>0$, precisely the supplier's
admissible scattering domain. In the center-of-momentum frame it
uses the invariant incoming flux $F$, the two-body measure $d\Phi_2$, and the
final-state factor $S_f=2$ for identical particles or $S_f=1$ for
distinguishable particles, integrated over the full labeled sphere. When
this coefficient is read phenomenologically, the initial preparation,
channel, threshold, and approximation are part of the model statement. No
universal error estimate for omitted terms is implied.

For the scalar examples, separately adopt the constant formal amplitudes
$\mathcal A=-\lambda$ for the quartic contact channel and $\mathcal G=G_E$
for the cubic parent decay, with the units and external normalization stated
at each use. The scalar scattering inputs lie on their stated positive
shells with a common total and the same strict threshold and positive-flux
conditions. For decay, the parent is $P_0=(\mathsf M_0,\mathbf0)$,
$\mathsf M_0>\mathsf M_1+\mathsf M_2$, and its two positive-shell daughters
sum to $P_0$. Their coefficient map is the one in
[[lem-qft-example-two-body-phase-space]]. If a rate $\Gamma$ is reported as
an energy width, the convention is explicitly $\Gamma_E:=\hbar\Gamma$; it
does not supply a survival law.

The readings above do not identify a formal coefficient with an exact
continuum cross section, probability, decay rate, or measured estimate. In
particular they do not construct an interacting continuum $S$-matrix or LSZ
limit, establish convergence of a perturbation series, bound loop or
soft-radiation effects, specify beam or detector cuts, resolve threshold
resummation, or reproduce the statistical analysis of an experiment. A
comparison with observations would require the actual apparatus, sampling,
calibration, uncertainty, and radiative-inclusiveness conditions. The
reported electron magnetic-moment measurements, including the Fan et al.
report listed in the source references, remain source-reported
empirical results and are not premises of this adoption.

pthm-qft-example-formal-scattering-decay.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ [[def-countable-choice]]. Use the fixed Cartesian
Minkowski chart $x=(ct,\mathbf x)$, the geometric metric
$\eta=(-,+,+,+)$, and the distinct algebraic contraction
$h=-\eta=(+,-,-,-)$ of [[def-qft-example-data]]. Let $m,M\geq0$ be the
electron and muon rest energies in joules. In this chart, a future energy
four-vector is
$q=(E,\mathbf q)\in\mathbb R^4$ with $E>0$; it has rest energy $\mathsf M\geq0$
when $h(q,q)=\mathsf M^2$. All four-vector components are in joules, and
$\mathbf q$ is $c$ times physical spatial momentum. Let $p_1,p_2$ be future electron
and positron energy four-vectors with rest energy $m$, and $k_1,k_2$ future
muon and antimuon energy four-vectors with rest energy $M$, satisfying
$p_1+p_2=k_1+k_2=P$ and
$$ s=h(P,P)>4\max(m^2,M^2). $$
By [[lem-qft-example-two-body-phase-space]], choose a proper orthochronous
$h$-Lorentz matrix $\Lambda\in GL(4,\mathbb R)$, meaning
$\Lambda^Th\Lambda=h$, $\det\Lambda=1$, and preservation of the future
causal cone $C_+:=\{(E,\mathbf q):E>0,\ h((E,\mathbf q),(E,\mathbf q))\geq0\}$,
with $\Lambda P=(\sqrt{s},\mathbf0)$.
Its boost construction supplies such a map because $P$ is future timelike.
The **center-of-momentum inertial chart** has coordinates
$x^{\rm CM}=\Lambda x$ on spacetime and corresponding four-vector components
$q^{\rm CM}=\Lambda q$; from here on, four-vector components are in that
chart, so $P=(\sqrt{s},\mathbf0)$. The strict threshold makes
$\mathbf p_1$ and $\mathbf k_1$ nonzero. Define the
scattering angle $\theta\in[0,\pi]$ by
$$\theta:=\arccos\!\left(\frac{\mathbf p_1\cdot\mathbf k_1}{|\mathbf p_1|\,|\mathbf k_1|}\right),$$
using the Euclidean inner product on $\mathbb R^3$.
Write $g=\sqrt{4\pi\alpha}>0$, as in
[[def-qft-example-data]], and
$$ \beta_e=\sqrt{1-\frac{4m^2}{s}},\qquad \beta_\mu=\sqrt{1-\frac{4M^2}{s}}. $$
For the selected formal one-photon tree coefficient, take equal incoherent
weight $1/4$ for the four initial spin-label pairs and sum over final spin
labels. Take the selected muon model charge to be $-e$ as well. Up to an
irrelevant common phase, its amplitude is
$$ \mathcal M_{\rm tree}=\frac{g^2}{s} [\bar v(p_2)\gamma^a u(p_1)] [\bar u(k_1)\gamma_a v(k_2)], $$
where the brackets denote the product of the two currents. This selected
formal amplitude adopts the current draft QFT-G02 line/vertex convention;
it is not an exact amplitude of a constructed continuum theory.

Conditional on this amplitude adoption and
[[post-qft-example-formal-observable-map]], the spin-averaged squared
coefficient is
$$ \overline{|\mathcal M_{\rm tree}|^2} =g^4[3-\beta_e^2-\beta_\mu^2 +\beta_e^2\beta_\mu^2\cos^2\theta], $$
The distinguishable-particle differential and total
cross-section coefficients are
$$ \frac{d\sigma_{\rm coeff}}{d\Omega} =\frac{\alpha^2(\hbar c)^2\beta_\mu}{4s\beta_e} [3-\beta_e^2-\beta_\mu^2+\beta_e^2\beta_\mu^2\cos^2\theta], $$
$$ \sigma_{\rm coeff} =\frac{\pi\alpha^2(\hbar c)^2}{s}\frac{\beta_\mu}{\beta_e} [3-\beta_e^2-\beta_\mu^2+\tfrac13\beta_e^2\beta_\mu^2]. $$
For $\delta=4m^2/s\leq1/2$, the ratio of this differential coefficient to
the coefficient at $m=0$ with the same $M,s,\theta$ belongs to
$[1,1+4\delta]$. This bound is only the incoming-electron-mass effect
within the selected tree coefficient.

The on-shell equations also give
$$ P_a\bar v(p_2)\gamma^a u(p_1)=0,\qquad P_a\bar u(k_1)\gamma^a v(k_2)=0. $$
These are the two current contractions for this finite external-spinor
calculation; they do not assert an all-orders or loop Ward theorem.

For the separate scalar conventions of
[[post-qft-example-formal-observable-map]], let $m_s\geq0$ be a scalar rest
energy, let the incoming $r_1,r_2$ and outgoing $l_1,l_2$ lie on the
positive $m_s$-shell, meaning each $(E,\mathbf q)$ has
$E=\sqrt{|\mathbf q|^2+m_s^2}>0$, and require
$r_1+r_2=l_1+l_2=P_s$ with $s=h(P_s,P_s)>4m_s^2$.
Evaluate in a proper orthochronous center-of-momentum chart taking $P_s$
to $(\sqrt{s},\mathbf0)$ as in [F4]. Let $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ be the dimensionless
constant quartic amplitude parameter. The identical-final full-sphere and
distinguishable total coefficients are respectively
$$ \sigma_{\rm coeff}^{\rm identical} =\frac{\lambda^2(\hbar c)^2}{32\pi s},\qquad \sigma_{\rm coeff}^{\rm distinguishable} =\frac{\lambda^2(\hbar c)^2}{16\pi s}. $$
For a parent at rest of energy $\mathsf M_0>2m_s$ and a constant identical
daughter amplitude $G_E$ in joules, take the daughters on the positive
$m_s$-shell with total $P_0=(\mathsf M_0,\mathbf0)$. The rate coefficient is
$$ \Gamma_{\rm coeff} =\frac{|G_E|^2}{32\pi\hbar\mathsf M_0} \sqrt{1-\frac{4m_s^2}{\mathsf M_0^2}}\quad[\mathrm{s}^{-1}]. $$
If an energy width is named, its convention is $\Gamma_E:=\hbar\Gamma_{\rm
coeff}$ in joules. None of these coefficient statements implies an exact
survival law. The QFT-G02 postulate is a current draft carrier; its use here
retains draft status and does not imply independent acceptance.

pthm-qft-example-soft-coherent-counts.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ [[def-countable-choice]]. Use the SI/natural
normalizations of [[def-qft-framework-units]] and
[[def-qft-example-data]], in particular the spacetime metric
$\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, the algebraic energy-momentum metric
$h=-\eta=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1)$, and the dimensionless coupling
$g_{\mathrm{em}}$ with $g_{\mathrm{em}}^2=4\pi\alpha$. For a finite nonempty
index set $i=1,\ldots,m$, take future massive energy-momentum vectors
$p_i=(E_i,\mathbf p_i)$ with components in joules and
$E_i^2-|\mathbf p_i|^2=M_i^2>0$. Put $\mathbf v_i=\mathbf p_i/E_i$, so
$|\mathbf v_i|<1$. Choose signs $s_i\in\{-1,+1\}$ and real dimensionless charges
$Q_i$ satisfying $\sum_i s_iQ_i=0$. These are prescribed current data, not
dynamical charged-particle trajectories.

For $\mathbf n\in S^2$, let $q=(\omega,\omega\mathbf n)$ with photon energy
$\omega>0$ in joules and define
$$p_i\cdot q:=E_i\omega-\mathbf p_i\cdot(\omega\mathbf n),\qquad J^\mu(q):=\sum_{i=1}^m s_iQ_i\frac{p_i^\mu}{p_i\cdot q},\qquad K^\mu(\mathbf n):=\omega J^\mu(\omega,\omega\mathbf n).$$
The dot in this current formula is $h$-contraction; in particular
$p_i\cdot q=\omega E_i(1-\mathbf v_i\cdot\mathbf n)>0$. Choose measurable
real orthonormal spatial polarizations $\epsilon_1(\mathbf n),\epsilon_2(\mathbf n)$
with $\mathbf n\cdot\epsilon_r(\mathbf n)=0$ almost everywhere. Put
$\epsilon_r^\mu=(0,\epsilon_r)$ and
$K\cdot\epsilon_r:=-\mathbf K\cdot\epsilon_r$. Define the finite nonnegative
angular coefficient
$$C:=\frac{g_{\mathrm{em}}^2}{2(2\pi)^3} \int_{S^2}\sum_{r=1}^{2}|K(\mathbf n)\cdot\epsilon_r(\mathbf n)|^2\,d\Omega.$$

For fixed energy cutoffs $0<\lambda<\Lambda<\infty$ in joules, define
$\mathfrak h_E=L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf q/[(2\pi)^3 2\omega];\mathbb C^2)$,
where $\omega=|\mathbf q|$, and
$$h_{\lambda,\Lambda,r}(\mathbf q) =g_{\mathrm{em}}J(q)\cdot\epsilon_r(\mathbf q/|\mathbf q|) \,\mathbf1_{\{\lambda<|\mathbf q|<\Lambda\}}.$$
The current draft mathematical supplier
[[thm-qft-example-soft-current-angular-coherent]] supplies the $\mathbb C^3$
transverse energy-space norm and unitary conversion. The measurable
orthonormal polarization frame gives the pointwise unitary identification
$h\mapsto\sum_{r=1}^2h_r\epsilon_r$ proved in step 3.1; composing it with
that conversion identifies $\mathfrak h_E$ with the positive transverse
one-particle space $\mathfrak h_T$ of [[def-qft-photon-transverse-space]]
by the unitary map below, where for $\mathbf k\ne0$ the notation
$\epsilon_r(\mathbf k)$ denotes the homogeneous extension
$\epsilon_r(\mathbf k/|\mathbf k|)$ of the supplied sphere frame:
$$(U_Eh)(\mathbf k)= \sqrt{\frac{(\hbar c)^2}{(2\pi)^3\,2|\mathbf k|}} \sum_{r=1}^{2}h_r(\hbar c\,\mathbf k)\epsilon_r(\mathbf k), \qquad \mathbf k\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}.$$
Here $\mathbf k$ is a wave vector in $\mathrm m^{-1}$ and
$\hbar c\,\mathbf k$ is the corresponding energy-momentum vector in joules.
Set $N_\gamma:=C\log(\Lambda/\lambda)$ and prepare the normalized coherent
vector in the free photon Fock space
$$\Psi_{\lambda,\Lambda} =e^{-N_\gamma/2}\bigoplus_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{(U_Eh_{\lambda,\Lambda})^{\otimes_s n}}{\sqrt{n!}} \in\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h_T),$$
where the $n=0$ term is the vacuum sector. Let $P_n$ be the number-sector
projection from [[def-qft-x03-photon-count-pvm]] and define
$p_n$ as the model probability assigned to outcome $n$ by the finite
two-outcome projective partition $\{\{n\},\mathbb R\setminus\{n\}\}$.
Then
$$p_n=e^{-N_\gamma}\frac{N_\gamma^n}{n!},\qquad n\in\mathbb N_0,$$
with $0^0:=1$; these probabilities sum to one, the mean photon count is
$N_\gamma$, and the vacuum probability is $e^{-N_\gamma}$. The expected
photon energy is
$$\langle\Psi_{\lambda,\Lambda},H_\gamma\Psi_{\lambda,\Lambda}\rangle =C(\Lambda-\lambda)\ \mathrm J,$$
for $H_\gamma=\hbar c\,d\Gamma(|\mathbf k|)$ of
[[post-qft-free-photon-model]]. If $C>0$, the family has no Fock-norm or
projective-ray limit as $\lambda\downarrow0$ (projective-ray convergence means
norm convergence after allowing a unit-modulus phase for each cutoff), although
its mean energy tends to the finite value $C\Lambda$.

For the prescribed one-charge rest-to-velocity current with final velocity
$v\hat{\mathbf z}$, $0<v<1$, take
$s_{\rm in}=-1$, $Q_{\rm in}=1$, $p_{\rm in}=(M,\mathbf0)$ and
$s_{\rm out}=+1$, $Q_{\rm out}=1$,
$p_{\rm out}=(M\gamma_v,M\gamma_v v\hat{\mathbf z})$, where $M>0$ is the
rest energy and $\gamma_v=(1-v^2)^{-1/2}$. The same coefficient is
$$C(v)=\frac{\alpha}{\pi} \left(\frac1v\log\frac{1+v}{1-v}-2\right)>0.$$
If $C>0$, the cutoff family has no Fock-norm or projective-ray limit as
$\lambda\downarrow0$; the proof below derives this from adjacent-shell
overlaps and does not use the supplier's separate conditional infrared-limit
clause. Its required norm and coherent-state inputs remain conditional on
the inspected draft supplier until its upstream inputs are current. This
prediction concerns only the constructed positive free coherent state and
its count PVM under the adopted physical assumptions. It does not infer that
a full interacting-QED scattering event emits that state or that a detector
realizes this PVM.

pthm-qft-qed-formal-ward.statement:
Use the coefficient convention of [[post-qft-formal-qed-coefficients]] and
formal ring of [[def-qft-qed-formal-ring]]. Let $\zeta$ denote finite graph
link data, $z$ a formal indeterminate, and
$K(z;\zeta)=K_0(\zeta)+zV(\zeta)\in M_d(\mathbb C\llbracket z\rrbracket)$
with $d\ge1$ and $K_0(\zeta)\in GL_d(\mathbb C)$. For each vertex-angle
tuple $\theta$, let $\zeta^\theta$ and the invertible diagonal matrix
$D_\theta$ be the finite gauge action and phase matrix of
[[def-qft-qed-finite-graph-gauge-data]]. Assume the coefficient matrices
satisfy
$$K_0(\zeta^\theta)=D_\theta K_0(\zeta)D_\theta^{-1},\qquad V(\zeta^\theta)=D_\theta V(\zeta)D_\theta^{-1}.$$
Let $S(z;\zeta)$ be the coefficientwise formal inverse specified by
[[def-qft-qed-formal-ring]]. Then
$$S(z;\zeta^\theta)=D_\theta S(z;\zeta)D_\theta^{-1},\qquad \det K(z;\zeta^\theta)=\det K(z;\zeta).$$
For a real vertex tuple $\theta$, put
$\Theta=\operatorname{diag}_{x\in X}(\theta_xI_r)$,
$\zeta^s:=\zeta^{s\theta}$, and $D_s:=D_{s\theta}=e^{is\Theta}$.
For any coefficient family $A_s=A(z;\zeta^s)$, write
$\delta A:=\left.\frac{d}{ds}A_s\right|_{s=0}$ coefficientwise.
Assume also that
$K_0(\zeta^s)$ and $V(\zeta^s)$ vary differentiably along the gauge orbit
$\zeta^s$. Coefficientwise differentiation then gives
$$\delta S=i[\Theta,S]=-S(\delta K)S.$$
These are finite/formal identities only; the formal variable is not assigned
a numerical value and no convergence is asserted.

For the tree-current clause, take $\mu>0$ and four future-shell momenta
$p,p',q,q'$ with $h(p,p)=h(p',p')=h(q,q)=h(q',q')=\mu^2$, in inverse-length
units, and put $k=p-p'=q'-q$. Let
$$J_1^a=\bar u(p')\gamma^a u(p),\qquad J_2^b=\bar u(q')\gamma^b u(q),$$
where $\bar u=u^\dagger\beta$ and the spinors satisfy the corresponding
positive-energy Dirac equations
$(\not p-\mu)u(p)=0$, $(\not p'-\mu)u(p')=0$,
$(\not q-\mu)u(q)=0$, $(\not q'-\mu)u(q')=0$ and their Dirac-adjoint
left equations, in the $h=-\eta$ convention of
[[post-qft-formal-qed-coefficients]]. For a finite scalar $c(k)$, set
$\Delta D_{ab}(k)=c(k)k_a k_b$. Then
$$J_1^a\Delta D_{ab}(k)J_2^b=0.$$
For either displayed conserved current, the contraction with a covector
$\epsilon_a$ is unchanged by $\epsilon_a\mapsto\epsilon_a+\rho k_a$ for
finite $\rho\in\mathbb C$. If $c(k)$ is a rational coefficient containing
$1/h(k,k)$, require $h(k,k)\ne0$ at the selected momentum; a distributional
$+i0$ boundary value is not a pointwise finite $c(k)$. The adopted off-shell
fermion coefficient has denominator $h(p,p)-\mu^2$ and is used only when
that denominator is nonzero. No internal-line singular product is used here.
The tree clause is limited to these explicit finite contractions and does not
assert gauge independence for arbitrary diagrams.

thm-qft-example-soft-current-angular-coh.statement:
This is a conditional mathematical theorem about a prescribed massive
charge-flow current and an exact free coherent-state model. The transverse
photon-space carrier [F2] and coherent-tail carrier [L1] are present at their
displayed interfaces. The coherent-tail proof now declares its exact
polar-coordinate and Euclidean surface-measure suppliers. Its weak-zero and
no-strong-limit conclusions are used under the hypotheses of [L1]. That
Statement contains no projective-ray conclusion; this item derives the ray
conclusion separately from the exact coherent overlap in step 7.1. Local
source repairs do not confer independent acceptance or replace current
native readiness reconciliation.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the constants and conventions of
[[def-qft-example-data]], and that the two current supplier interfaces [F2]
and [L1] hold exactly as stated below. Let $I$ be a finite, possibly empty,
set of legs with energies $E_i>0$ in joules, dimensionless velocities
$v_i=\mathbf v_{i,\rm phys}/c\in\mathbb R^3$ with $|v_i|<1$, dimensionless charges $Q_i\in\mathbb R$,
signs $\eta_i\in\{-1,1\}$, and charge balance
$\sum_{i\in I}\eta_iQ_i=0$. Use $h=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1)$ for
algebraic four-vector contractions. For $n\in S^2$ and energy
$\omega>0$ in joules, put
$$ p_i=E_i(1,v_i),\qquad q=\omega(1,n),\qquad K(n)=\sum_{i\in I}\eta_iQ_i\frac{(1,v_i)}{1-v_i\cdot n}. $$
Define the prescribed current
$J(q)=\sum_{i\in I}\eta_iQ_i\,p_i/h(p_i,q)$. Since
$h(p_i,q)=E_i\omega(1-v_i\cdot n)>0$, this equals $K(n)/\omega$.
Let $P_T(n)=I-n\otimes n$ and
$K_\perp(n)=P_T(n)\mathbf K(n)$. Define $d\Omega$ as Euclidean chart
surface measure on $S^2$ and
$$ C=\frac{g^2}{2(2\pi)^3}\int_{S^2}|K_\perp(n)|^2\,d\Omega(n)\ge0, \qquad h_\lambda(\mathbf q)=g\frac{K_\perp(n)}{\omega} \mathbf1_{\{\lambda<\omega<\Lambda\}}, \quad 0<\lambda<\Lambda, $$
where $g>0$ is the dimensionless coupling of [[def-qft-example-data]] and
$\lambda,\Lambda$ are energy cutoffs in joules. Write $\mathbf q=\omega n$ for the spatial energy coordinate, distinct from
the four-vector $q=(\omega,\mathbf q)$ above, and interpret $h_\lambda$
as a function of $\mathbf q$. Define
$\mathcal H_{E,T}:=\{h\in L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf q/[(2\pi)^3 2|\mathbf q|];\mathbb C^3):\mathbf q\cdot h(\mathbf q)=0\ {\rm a.e.}\}$,
with the componentwise Hermitian integral pairing linear in its second
variable. On this energy-coordinate transverse Hilbert space the exact norm is
$$ N_\lambda=\|h_\lambda\|^2=C\log(\Lambda/\lambda). $$
The energy-coordinate wavefunction has units $\mathrm J^{-1}$ and its
one-particle measure has units $\mathrm J^2$, so $N_\lambda$ and $C$ are
dimensionless; its value at $q=0$ is immaterial to this $L^2$ vector.
Under the canonical unitary $U:\mathcal H_{E,T}\to\mathcal H_T$ specified and proved in step 3.1,
the same vector is
$$ f_\lambda(k)=\mathbf1_{\{\lambda/(\hbar c)<|k|<\Lambda/(\hbar c)\}} |k|^{-3/2}b(k/|k|),\qquad b(n)=\frac{gK_\perp(n)}{\sqrt{2(2\pi)^3}},\qquad \int_{S^2}|b|^2\,d\Omega=C. $$
The normalized coherent vector
$\Psi_\lambda=W(-i\sqrt2 f_\lambda)\Omega
=e^{-N_\lambda/2}\epsilon(f_\lambda)$ has squared norm in sector $m$
$$ s_m=e^{-N_\lambda}\frac{N_\lambda^m}{m!},\qquad \sum_{m\ge0}s_m=1,\qquad \sum_{m\ge0}m s_m=N_\lambda. $$
These are Hilbert-space sector norms and their index sum; no measured
probability is asserted. For the free photon energy operator
$H_\gamma=\hbar c\,d\Gamma(|k|)$, $\Psi_\lambda$ is in its operator domain
and its quadratic expectation is $C(\Lambda-\lambda)$ joules.

If $C=0$, $f_\lambda=0$ almost everywhere and $\Psi_\lambda=\Omega$ for each
cutoff. If $C>0$, the exact hypotheses of the current [L1] hold with
$\epsilon=\lambda/(\hbar c)$, $\kappa=\Lambda/(\hbar c)$ and the displayed
nonzero transverse angular function $b$. Conditional on [L1], the family has
no strong Fock-vector limit and converges weakly to zero, while its free
energy expectation stays bounded. For unit Fock vectors define their projective-ray distance by
$d([u],[v]):=\inf_{|z|=1}\|u-zv\|$; projective convergence means convergence
in this distance, equivalently norm convergence to a fixed unit vector after
allowing a unit-modulus phase at each cutoff. Step 7.1 proves separately that
these rays have no projective limit, including after arbitrary phase choices. This is
not a result about full interacting QED, universal charged sectors,
detector-inclusive observables, or measured photon statistics.
